title: Father! Thy Paternal Care
description: Father! Thy Paternal Care in Tonic Solfa to WATCHMAN, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 22, “Every Good Gift from the Father”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WATCHMAN; any other Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther! Thy pa-ter-nal care Has my guar-dian been, my guide: Ev-ery hal-lowed wish and prayer Has Thy hand of love sup-plied: Thine is ev-ery thought of bliss, Left by hours and days gone by; Ev-ery hope Thine off-spring is, Beam-ing from fu-tu-ri-ty.

lines: Has my guardian been, my guide:
Has Thy hand of love supplied:
Thine is every thought of bliss,
Left by hours and days gone by;
These, — and all life's holiest things,
And its fairest, — all are Thine.
And for all, my hymns shall rise
Trusting still, through ill and good,
Fixed, and cheered, and counselled there.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WATCHMAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
